facts.text: The package supports the NI PXIe-5160, 5164 and 5110 and states that it requires Windows and NI hardware
Adaptive sampling raises the sample rate towards 30 times the signal frequency and is capped at 1.25 GS/s
The hardware backend imports the niscope package
DirectBackend drives real NI oscilloscopes through the niscope API
scan_devices opens niscope.Session(name, reset_device=False) for each candidate PXI slot and reads the model, channel count and maximum rates
open_device opens niscope.Session(resource_name, reset_device=False) for the selected scope
configure_channel writes channel_enabled, vertical_range, vertical_offset, vertical_coupling, probe_attenuation and input_impedance
configure_trigger writes the trigger source, level and slope, and configure_horizontal writes min_sample_rate, horz_min_num_pts, horz_num_records, horz_record_ref_position and horz_enforce_realtime
read_waveform fetches num_samples and downsamples the time and voltage arrays to at most 2000 points
measure_waveform fetches num_samples and returns rounded frequency, period, amplitude, RMS, minimum, maximum, mean, rise time, fall time, duty cycle, sample count and sample rate

get_current_config reports the model, the horizontal sample rate, record length and actual sample rate, the trigger source, level and slope, and per-channel enabled, vertical range, offset, coupling, probe attenuation and input impedance
ChannelConfig carries vertical_range in Vpp, vertical_offset in V, vertical_coupling AC/DC/GND, probe_attenuation, input_impedance in ohms and bandwidth_filter
TriggerConfig carries source, level, slope, coupling, holdoff and type
HorizontalConfig carries min_sample_rate, min_num_pts, num_records, ref_position, enforce_realtime and acquisition_type
The configure_scope help text names the channel, horizontal and trigger settings and their units
The help text lists vertical_range common values 0.1-50 Vpp, input impedance 50 or 1000000 ohm, and min_sample_rate common values 1e6-1.25e9 S/s
main() serves the MCP server over get_backend('direct')
